note: Wiki pages and onboarding lessons. Every rule here must match Balance.json and the simulation (Simulator.cs, Layout.cs). Live numbers (costs, kW, sizes) are added by code from Balance.json. Lessons marked required must be seen once before the levels that list them in 'needs'; after that they can be skipped or replayed from the Wiki. The teacher's lesson was removed on 2026-11-15: Tutorial 2 teaches its content through the crew. 'training' is Tutorial 2: one step at a time, each done when its 'done' condition holds (Training.cs); 'target' is what the arrow points at; 'start' begins an event.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Hi, Commander! I'm Priya, the engineer. Welcome to our practice base at the space agency.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Time is stopped, so nothing moves yet. Press Play at the top right to start the clock.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Time is running! Press the same button to pause. You can still build and give orders while paused.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: This button runs time 2× or 4× faster. Speed up when the base is calm.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Let's build! The Habitat is the crew's home. Pick its card. Glowing green tiles are good spots.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: The Habitat cost Supplies. Every building does. Your Supplies are at the end of the top bar.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Next, Air Support. It uses power to make the air we breathe. Put it right next to the Habitat.
training.goal: Build Air Support next to the Habitat.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Both need power. Solar Arrays turn sunlight into power. Bright ground is best.
training.goal: Build a Solar Array on bright ground.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: See Power at the top? Power in must beat power out, so it should show +.
training.goal: Add Solar Arrays until Power shows +.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: A Battery stores spare power for later. Within 2 tiles of a Solar Array, no power is wasted.
training.goal: Build a Battery near a Solar Array.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Air, Water and Food keep us alive. If any one of them reaches 0, the mission ends!

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: An empty Battery alone is fine. If Habitat or Air Support lose power for {outage}, the mission ends.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: When something runs low, a ring and an arrow point at it. Hover any number to learn more.

training.speaker: geologist
training.text: Hi, I'm Yuki, the geologist! I explore outside and look for minerals and ice.

training.speaker: geologist
training.text: When I'm far away, you call me on the Radio Dish. It needs power to work.

training.speaker: geologist
training.text: My rover brings soil, then water. Build its garage near the brown soil dots.
training.goal: Build the Rover Garage near soil.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: The Radio Dish and the rover use power too. Keep Power at +.

training.speaker: botanist
training.text: Hello! I'm Mateo, the botanist. I grow our food in the Greenhouse.

training.speaker: botanist
training.text: My Greenhouse needs 6 bags of soil, and rover trips take time. Let time run, fast if you like!
training.goal: Press Play to let time run.

training.speaker: botanist
training.text: Watch Soil at the top. The rover brings 2 bags on each trip.

training.speaker: botanist
training.text: Now my Greenhouse! Put it next to Air Support. They share air pipes and save power.
training.goal: Build the Greenhouse next to Air Support.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Plants need power too. If Power shows −, add a Solar Array.

training.speaker: botanist
training.text: Plants drink water, and now the rover brings it. Let's wait for the first harvest!

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Uh oh, a long shadow! Less sun means less power. Let's save some. Click the Greenhouse.
training.goal: Click the Greenhouse on the map.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Press Turn off. The plants can rest. Air Support always stays on.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Now the Battery helps us. When power out beats power in, it drains. Wait for the sun.
training.goal: Wait for the shadow to pass.

training.speaker: botanist
training.text: The sun is back! Please turn my Greenhouse on again.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: You got through the dark, so a second Battery is unlocked. Put it near a Solar Array.

training.speaker: geologist
training.text: Storm warning! Solar particles arrive in 12 hours, and I'm outside! First, stop time.

training.speaker: geologist
training.text: Time stands still, but you can still give orders. Call me in with the Radio Dish!

training.speaker: geologist
training.text: Now build the Shelter within 2 tiles of the Habitat. It shields us from particles.
training.goal: Build the Shelter near the Habitat.

training.speaker: geologist
training.text: A new Shelter starts switched off to save power. Turn it on now!

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: All set. Press Play to start time again.

training.speaker: geologist
training.text: We're in the Shelter. If Crew safety stays low too long, the mission ends. Wait for the all clear.
training.goal: Stay safe until the storm ends.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: Forgot something? The Wiki explains every building, resource and event. Open it any time.

training.speaker: geologist
training.text: Real missions have a time limit. This flag counts down to the inspection.

training.speaker: botanist
training.text: At inspection, mission control grades your base: S, A, B or C. Running out of time is not failing.

training.speaker: engineer
training.text: {level} lasts {mission}: about {minutes} minutes at 1×. Pause to think, speed up when it's calm.

wiki.title: How to play
wiki.summary: Six steps to a working base.

rows.text: 1. Place the Habitat first. All other buildings must be within 6 tiles of it.
2. Put Air Support next to the Habitat (1 tile or less). It makes air.
3. Build Solar Arrays on bright ground. Power in must beat power out.
4. Put a Battery within 2 tiles of your Solar Arrays to save spare power.
5. A Rover Garage near soil and water fetches soil for the Greenhouse.
6. Time starts when you press Play. Pause any time to think. When time runs out, your base is inspected. That is not a failure.

wiki.title: Reading the screen
wiki.summary: Where everything is.

rows.text: Top bar: your resources. Hover over or tap a number to learn more.
Top right: the time, Pause, the speed button (1×, 2×, 4×) and the inspection countdown.
Left: your crew. Click a crew member to talk. The Wiki button is below them.
Right, top: Information. Warnings and messages for the commander.
Right, bottom: Objectives. Each one gets a tick when it is done.
Bottom: Buildings. Pick one, then click the map.

wiki.title: Controls
wiki.summary: Mouse first. Touch works too.

rows.text: Click a building card, then click the map. Right-click or press Cancel to stop.
Click a building on the map to see what it needs. Some can be turned off.
Space: pause or resume. H: open this Wiki. Esc: menu.

wiki.title: What ends a mission
wiki.summary: Keep Air, Water and Food above 0 and the Habitat powered.

rows.text: Air at 0: the mission stops.
Water at 0: the mission stops.
Food at 0: the mission stops.
Habitat or Air Support without power for 10 hours: the mission stops. An empty Battery alone does not stop it.
Crew safety below 50% for 2 hours in a solar storm: the mission stops.
The inspection at the end of the countdown is not a failure. It gives your grade.

wiki.title: Habitat
wiki.summary: Home for the crew. Build it first.
wiki.best: Pick a place with bright ground nearby. Every other building must be within 6 tiles of it.

rows.text: The crew lives here. Your base grows around it.
Uses power all the time. If it has no power for 10 hours, the mission stops.
Put Air Support within 1 tile of it for full air.

wiki.title: Solar Array
wiki.summary: Turns sunlight into power.
wiki.best: Bright ground, within 2 tiles of a Battery. Far from a Battery, a long cable wastes 30% of its power.

rows.text: Makes up to 3 kW in full sun. Darker ground makes less.
Spare power goes into the Battery.
Shadows and dust storms lower its power. A solar storm does not.

wiki.title: Battery
wiki.summary: Saves spare power for later.
wiki.best: Within 2 tiles of your Solar Arrays: short cables waste no power.

rows.text: Charges when power in beats power out. Gives power back when it runs short.
It can charge or give at most 5 kW at a time.
You start with one. A second one unlocks after your first long shadow or dust storm.

wiki.title: Air Support
wiki.summary: Makes air for the crew to breathe.
wiki.best: Next to the Habitat (1 tile or less). A Greenhouse right next to it saves 1 kW.

rows.text: Within 1 tile of the Habitat, it adds 2 hours of air every hour. Farther away, a long air pipe halves that.
Needs power. Without power, the air goes down 1 hour every hour.
If the air runs out, the mission stops. Never let it lose power.

wiki.title: Radio Dish
wiki.summary: Lets you talk to your crew and Earth.

rows.text: You need it to call Yuki back to base in a solar storm.
Needs power. It is the first thing switched off when power runs short.

wiki.title: Greenhouse
wiki.summary: Grows food. Needs soil, power and water.
wiki.best: Right next to Air Support (1 tile): the plants help clean the air, so Air Support uses 1 kW less.

rows.text: Costs 6 bags of soil. The rover brings soil.
Grows half a meal every hour and adds a little air.
Uses water, but recycles most of it. With no water, it stops growing.
Your first harvest brings 30 supplies. If the Shelter is locked, it unlocks it.

wiki.title: Shelter
wiki.summary: Protects the crew from solar particles.
wiki.best: Within 2 tiles of the Habitat. Farther away, it only half protects the crew.

rows.text: When it is switched on and powered, the crew inside is safe from storm particles.
It starts switched off. Turn it on when a storm warning comes.
Unlocks after your first harvest.

wiki.title: Rover Garage
wiki.summary: Its rover fetches soil, then water.
wiki.best: Within 2 tiles of soil and 3 tiles of water. Short trips are faster. Farther than 8 tiles, the rover cannot go.

rows.text: First it brings soil, 2 bags a trip, until you have enough for the Greenhouse.
Then it brings water, 1.5 L a trip.
Needs power. It switches off early when power runs short.

wiki.title: Power
wiki.summary: Power in from Solar Arrays, minus power out to buildings.

rows.text: Made by Solar Arrays. Measured in kW.
Spare power charges the Battery.
When power runs short, the base switches off: Radio Dish and Rover Garage, then Greenhouse, then Shelter. Habitat and Air Support stay on longest.

wiki.title: Battery
wiki.summary: Power saved for later, in kWh.

rows.text: Each Battery holds 12 kWh.
It fills when you have spare power and empties when you do not.

wiki.title: Air
wiki.summary: Hours of air (oxygen) left for the crew.

rows.text: Air Support makes it. The most you can store is 36 hours.
A working Greenhouse adds a little air too.
Without powered Air Support, air drops 1 hour every hour. At 0, the mission stops.

wiki.title: Water
wiki.summary: Litres of water for drinking and plants.

rows.text: The crew drinks a little every hour.
The Greenhouse uses some, but recycles most.
The rover brings more: ice on the Moon, wet clay on Mars. At 0, the mission stops.

wiki.title: Food
wiki.summary: Meals left for the crew.

rows.text: Three crew eat 3 meals a day each: 9 a day.
The Greenhouse grows more. At 0, the mission stops.

wiki.title: Soil
wiki.summary: Bags of soil for the Greenhouse.

rows.text: The rover brings soil from brown tiles. You can keep up to 12 bags.
The Greenhouse needs 6 bags to build.

wiki.title: Crew safety
wiki.summary: How safe the crew is from solar particles.

rows.text: Drops in a solar storm if someone is outside, or the Shelter is off or has no power.
Comes back slowly when everyone is safe. Below 50% for 2 hours, the mission stops.

wiki.title: Supplies
wiki.summary: Building materials. Every building costs supplies.

rows.text: Supply landers bring more. Your first harvest brings 30.
Removing a building gives its supplies back. Fixing a broken Solar Array costs 5.

wiki.title: Buildings that help each other
wiki.summary: Where you build changes how well it works.

rows.text: Solar Array within 2 tiles of a Battery: no power lost in the cable.
Air Support within 1 tile of the Habitat: full air. Farther: half.
Greenhouse next to Air Support: Air Support uses 1 kW less.
Shelter within 2 tiles of the Habitat: full protection.
Rover Garage near soil and water: faster trips.
Good links also raise the Layout part of your grade.

wiki.title: What makes what
wiki.summary: Each building turns some resources into others.

rows.text: Sunlight makes power. Power runs every other building.
Air Support: power makes air.
Rover Garage: power makes soil trips, then water trips.
Greenhouse: soil (to build), power and water make food and a little air.
Radio Dish: power lets you call the crew.
Shelter: power keeps the crew safe in a storm.

wiki.title: Priya, Engineer
wiki.summary: Careful planner. Looks after power.

rows.text: Looks after Solar Arrays and the Battery.
Needs from you: power in bigger than power out. Switch off what can wait.

wiki.title: Mateo, Botanist
wiki.summary: Cheerful plant lover. Grows the food.

rows.text: Runs the Greenhouse.
Needs from you: soil and water from the rover, and power for the Greenhouse.

wiki.title: Yuki, Geologist
wiki.summary: Curious explorer. Drives the rover and studies rocks.

rows.text: Explores outside and searches for minerals and ice.
Needs from you: a powered Radio Dish, so you can call her in.
In a solar storm she is outside. Call her in early.

wiki.title: Solar storm
wiki.summary: Fast particles from the Sun. Mission control warns you first.

rows.text: The warning comes about 12 hours before the particles arrive.
1. Call Yuki in. The Radio Dish needs power.
2. Switch on the Shelter and keep it powered.
3. Short on power? Rest the Greenhouse.
The Sun still shines. Solar Arrays keep working.
If you do not call her, Yuki heads back 1 hour after the particles arrive, and crew safety drops.

wiki.title: Long shadow and dust storm
wiki.summary: Less sun for a while. Solar Arrays make less power.

rows.text: A warning comes 8 hours before. Charge the Battery.
Rest the Greenhouse if power runs short.
Getting through the first one unlocks a second Battery.

wiki.title: Other events
wiki.summary: Landers, harvests, sunrise and space rocks.

rows.text: Supply lander: brings more supplies.
First harvest: 30 supplies.
Space rock: breaks a Solar Array. Fix it for 5 supplies.
Sunrise: sunlight creeps over the ridge and solar power climbs.

wiki.title: Inspection and grades
wiki.summary: When time runs out, mission control grades your base.

rows.text: The countdown at the top right shows when the inspection comes.
Grades: S 81+, A 61+, B 31+, C 0+. Running out of time is never a failure.
Points come from goals, layout, crew safety, reserves and steady power.

wiki.title: Reading the map
wiki.summary: Bright ground, soil, water and rocks.

rows.text: Brighter ground gets more sun, so Solar Arrays make more power there.
Brown dots: soft soil for the rover.
Blue dots: ice on the Moon. Teal dots: wet clay on Mars.
Dark rocks and craters: you cannot build there.
While placing, the dark area is outside your base. You cannot build there.
Green glow: a suggested spot. It is a tip, not a rule.

wiki.title: Tutorial 2: Practice Base
wiki.summary: Priya, Yuki and Mateo show you a whole mission. Play it again from Story Mode.

rows.text: Priya: Play starts time, the same button pauses, the speed button runs 2× or 4×.
Priya: Habitat, Air Support, Solar Arrays, Battery. Keep Power at +.
Air, Water or Food at 0 ends a mission. A ring and an arrow show what runs low.
Yuki: the Radio Dish keeps you in contact. Her rover brings soil, then water.
Mateo: the Greenhouse needs 6 soil and sits next to Air Support.
Long shadow: less sun. Turn off the Greenhouse to save power.
Storm warning: Pause, call Yuki in, switch on the Shelter, press Play.
Missions have a time limit. At inspection you get a grade: S, A, B or C.

wiki.title: Facts you found
wiki.summary: A science fact pops up the first time something happens. Every fact you find is kept here.
wiki.source: Each fact lists its own source.

rows.text: Build, harvest and live through storms to find more. Free Build storms show new real data.

wiki.title: Real data in this game
wiki.summary: Where each real dataset is used. Everything else is made up for play.
wiki.source: DATA_SOURCES.md and SCIENCE_SOURCES.md in the project list every link and date.

rows.text: NASA DONKI: real solar storms (flare, gas cloud, particles, Kp). Storm warnings and storm facts.
NASA OSDR RadLab: Space Station radiation on 11 May 2024. A storm fact.
NASA OSDR: 12 real studies on plants, bodies and radiation. Wiki and results screen.
LRO LOLA (NASA PDS): sunlight near the Moon's south pole. The Moon map and Moon facts.
MGS MOLA (NASA PDS): heights around Jezero crater. The Mars map.
NASA POWER: sunlight in Mississauga. The sunrise fact.
Canadian Space Agency: food in space, Tomatosphere, David Saint-Jacques. Plant facts.
NASA pages: life support, radio delay, Artemis I, Mars rovers, space rocks. Fact cards.
Made up for play: kW, kWh, costs, recycling, air hours, crew safety and event timing.
Saved data, not live: the game works offline. Not endorsed by NASA or CSA.

wiki.title: Real solar storms
wiki.summary: Every solar storm in this game copies a real one from NASA's DONKI database.
wiki.source: NASA CCMC DONKI (ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/tools/DONKI); NASA Science, the most intense solar storm in decades (16 May 2024).

rows.text: Story levels use the X5.8 flare of 11 May 2024. Free Build picks one of 8 real storms.
Each storm links a flare, a cloud of solar gas (a CME) and fast particles (SEP).
The order of events is real. Warning hours and crew effects are made up.
Kp measures storms on Earth, from 0 to 9. It is never a Moon dose.
In May 2024, auroras were seen as far south as the southern U.S.

wiki.title: Radiation and your body
wiki.summary: Why the Shelter matters, from real NASA research.
wiki.source: NASA Human Research Program; NASA Artemis I radiation article (9 Oct 2024); George et al. 2024, Nature 634, 48-52; NASA OSDR.

rows.text: A gray measures radiation energy the body takes in. A microgray is a millionth of one.
The Space Station is inside Earth's magnetic field. Its readings are not Moon doses.
Artemis I: radiation inside Orion varied by location. Each spot had different shielding.
When Orion turned during an engine burn, radiation dropped by nearly half.
Two test dummies, Helga and Zohar, flew on Artemis I. Zohar wore a radiation vest.
Studies marked Ground Study used space-like radiation made on Earth.

wiki.title: Plants in space
wiki.summary: Real space gardens, and why crews far from Earth need them.
wiki.source: NASA Veg-04/Veg-05 page; NASA OSDR; Canadian Space Agency (© Canadian Space Agency).

rows.text: Veg-04 tested mizuna mustard. Veg-05 grew dwarf tomatoes.
In this game, the Greenhouse's food, water and air numbers are made up.

wiki.title: Air, water and radio
wiki.summary: How real crews breathe, drink and call home.
wiki.source: NASA ECLSS page (4 April 2025); NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet; NASA Moon to Mars white paper (2023); NASA Johnson HVIT.

rows.text: The Space Station removes carbon dioxide with sieves that sort gases by size.
Air hours, water use and recycling numbers in this game are made up.

wiki.title: The Moon's south pole
wiki.summary: Our Moon map is a real crop near the Moon's south pole.
wiki.source: LRO LOLA illumination (Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211); NASA SVS; NASA NSSDC; NASA POWER.

rows.text: 20 x 15 tiles near Shackleton crater, about 5.7 km from the pole.
Tile brightness is long-term average sunlight, not live shadows.
The game puts ice in every dark tile. Real dark craters do not all hold ice.
Free Build and Tutorial 2 use made-up maps.

wiki.title: Mars at Jezero
wiki.summary: Our Mars map is real heights around Jezero crater.
wiki.source: MGS MOLA MEGDR (NASA PDS); NASA JPL Mars 2020 press kit; NASA NSSDC Mars Fact Sheet; NASA JPL MOXIE.

rows.text: Each tile is about 3.7 km wide. Steep tiles are blocked.
Lake mud and wet clay tiles are picked for play, not mapped minerals.
Mars solar power in this game is softened to 60% of the Moon's.
